sections.title: Course Staff and Content Structure
sections.description: The instructor introduces the teaching staff and explains the divide between discrete math and probability.

sections.title: Mathematical Conjectures and Logistics
sections.description: Motivational math problems regarding prime numbers and code correctness accompany a review of course communication channels.

sections.title: Perspectives on Mathematical Truth
sections.description: The instructor defines the specific level of axiomatic rigor and truth required for computer science proofs.

sections.title: Discrete Versus Continuous Systems
sections.description: The discussion explores the distinction between discrete and continuous systems as well as various course applications.

sections.title: Success Strategies and Grading Policies
sections.description: Students learn about the importance of homework, collaboration, and various grading options for the semester.

sections.title: Formal Definitions and Integer Notation
sections.description: The lecture provides the first rigorous mathematical definitions and formal notation for working with integers.

sections.title: Proof for the Sum of Even Integers
sections.description: A step-by-step demonstration shows how to prove that the sum of two even integers remains even.

sections.title: Proof for the Sum of Odd Integers
sections.description: Students collaborate on a proof regarding the sum of two odd integers using formal definitions.

sections.title: Propositions and Truth Values
sections.description: The class transitions to propositional logic by defining statements that are strictly true or false.

sections.title: Predicates and Variable Quantifiers
sections.description: New notation introduces predicates and quantifiers that specify the range of variables in mathematical statements.

sections.title: Nested Quantifiers and Variable Order
sections.description: Examples demonstrate how the specific order of universal and existential quantifiers significantly alters a statement's meaning.

sections.title: Quantifier Negation and Fermat's Last Theorem
sections.description: The lecture concludes with the negation of quantified statements and a reference to Fermat's Last Theorem.
